records.name: replay-risk authorization by stable intent identity — TWO rules for two key states (GPT v4 §9): a key with an UNKNOWN attempt admits a replay only under REPLAY_RISK_AUTHORIZED (a pre-outcome authorization fact, NOT a terminal; the operator accepts that the prior attempt may already have landed); a key that is SATISFIED (COMMITTED, or SUPERSEDED because another attempt satisfied it) is refused as already satisfied and the existing satisfaction is returned — the risk fact does not license repeating a done intent; another physical effect is a NEW intent (new effect_key / intent_id, repeat_of = the old intent, fresh approval and authority; a product-level "knowingly repeat" operation would be REPEAT_INTENT_AUTHORIZED, never the uncertainty override); a key whose attempts all settled FAILED-absent is free. ampd today admits a same-key replay under a new attempt id without consulting the key at all — duplicate-safety rests entirely on the far side
